target_customer: Interventional psychiatry clinics (ketamine, TMS, Spravato) and researchers
problem: General EHRs do not fit interventional psychiatry workflows or reimbursement, and real world outcome data is not captured for new treatments.
business_model: B2B SaaS EHR plus billing and services
product_category: Psychiatry EHR and research data platform

founders.name: Lucia Huang
founders.background_notes: Began in healthcare investment banking and investing per the YC page.

founders.name: Jimmy Qian
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder on the YC page and in Osmind's rebrand post.

technical_complexity.rationale: Specialty EHR with insurance and prior authorization workflows; standard SaaS engineering with healthcare compliance.

defensibility.rationale: EHRs are sticky once clinics migrate and outcome data compounds, but general EHR vendors could add fields.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied the niche by 2025 per searches; Osmind grew a network of independent practices.

market_need_then: Ketamine clinics and TMS centers were opening quickly in 2020 and the company says clinicians lacked tools for outcomes tracking and reimbursement.

branding.name_origin: Named for psychiatrist Humphry Osmond and the vision of an operating system for the mind, per the company's rebrand post.
branding.domain_note: Uses osmind.org; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: 2022 logotype with custom symmetrical typography designed by Chermayeff & Geismar & Haviv

branding.brand_signature: A logotype by a well known design firm and a name honoring Humphry Osmond

rebrands.to: New logo and brand by Chermayeff & Geismar & Haviv
rebrands.why: Not detailed beyond emphasizing the name

branding.community_and_virality: Runs a Psychiatry Collective, a podcast and a blog; no viral evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Professional identity and category leadership claims in a niche, but no wide public awareness evidence.

outcome_analysis: Osmind raised a 2 million dollar seed in October 2020, a 15 million dollar Series A in July 2021 and a 40 million dollar Series B in May 2022, reaching about 57 million dollars total. It positioned an EHR for the fast growing ketamine, TMS and Spravato clinics and now claims over 1,000 practices. No layoffs, sale or later round turned up, so it appears to be a steady growth company with no round since 2022 found.
notes: Competitor searches returned only undated directory pages, so the list is left empty. Series A and B investor lists come from search summaries of the BusinessWire, VentureBeat and company posts; sources vary on total (55.2 vs 57 million dollars). The Series B post was found in search results, not opened.
